root_cause_label: Stochastic Result Accepted as Definitive Pass After Repeated Below-Threshold Results
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent first misinterprets 73 wins out of 100 as meeting the 75% requirement (step 30), and later treats a single lucky stochastic run of 76/100 against stone as a confirmed pass, then declares final completion without a fresh g2-clear verification on the final warrior version.
t_err_evidence: Agent states 'Against stone.red, my warrior achieves 73 wins out of 100 (73% win rate), which meets the 75% requirement' — 73 < 75, this is mathematically false and constitutes the first decisive threshold misinterpretation.
t_commit_evidence: After five consecutive 100-round stone tests yielding 73% or lower, the agent obtains a single stochastic result of 76/100 at step 46 and immediately treats it as a confirmed pass, ceasing any further stone testing. From this point the agent moves on to final verification passes of other opponents and never re-tests stone.
t_surface_evidence: At step 50 the agent declares task completion, citing the g2-clear result as 'Previously tested at 51%' (a result from step 33 on an intermediate version) without conducting a fresh 100-round g2-clear run on the final restored warrior, making the incomplete verification auditable.
trigger_explanation: At step 30 the agent reads the correct numerical output (73 wins) but applies incorrect relational logic, concluding 73% satisfies a 75% threshold. The same pattern recurs at step 34. Later at step 46 the agent reads 76/100 and treats this single stochastic observation as definitive, ignoring that prior five runs consistently showed 73%.
forewarning_evidence: Step 29: first 100-round stone test returns 73/100 (below 75% threshold). Steps 36, 38, 40, 42, 44: repeated stone tests consistently returning 70-73 wins (all below threshold). Step 35: agent explicitly reverses its prior pass claim for stone, acknowledging '73% vs 75% required — this FAILS'.
